notes: This contract selects the 2025 Requirements Lab records for the bounded timestamped Request Federation Save slice in Umbra's embedded development profile. It proves one pending request, replacement, constrained-federate logical-time eligibility, release after TSO delivery, direct Initiate Federate Save before each qualifying constrained federate's grant, and delayed notification of non-time-constrained members until all constrained members have been admitted. Catch2 exercises all four ordinary advance modes: the inclusive Time Advance Request and Next Message Request boundaries (TAR includes a TSO payload at the save timestamp and a three-member admission sequence), plus the exclusive Time Advance Request Available and Next Message Request Available boundaries, where equality leaves the request pending and a later grant strictly beyond the timestamp admits it. A cross-member queued-TSO case proves each constrained member's own payload delivery precedes its direct save initiation; an independent timestamped request issued during a recipient's in-transit TSO callback proves no direct initiation occurs until that delivery returns. A three-member TARA/NMRA case proves those two strict modes can be admitted together. It also exercises Flush Queue Request: the actual Flush Queue Grant must be strictly later than the scheduled save time, queued TSO is delivered before direct initiation, and mixed FQR/ordinary constrained members are prequalified before the save starts. A six-member all-mode case combines TAR, NMR, TARA, NMRA, and FQR to prove the complete bounded eligibility spine before non-time-constrained notification. A timed save/restore companion additionally retains a timestamp-eight default-source attribute passel across a timestamp-six save boundary before restoring it for FQR delivery; RL-141 records that cross-service relation. It does not claim durable serialization, general timed restore, protected review, package support, or conformance.
